title: Token-aware retry budgets, backoff presets, and idempotency key ergonomics for stream-first SDKs
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: As more customers adopt streaming and chunked response patterns, we observe duplicated work and surprising costs when client libraries retry streaming requests. There is no single cross-language guidance that ties retry budgets to token costs, recommends safe idempotency key shapes for chunked/streamed payloads, and gives sensible defaults for backoff jitter that minimize thundering herd without increasing latency for small interactive calls.

Goal: Ship a cross-SDK spec and reference implementation for Python/TypeScript/Go that: 1) defines token-aware retry budgets and per-request retry caps for generation/streaming endpoints; 2) proposes backoff presets (fast, balanced, conservative) with deterministic jitter approach; 3) standardizes idempotency key semantics across unary and streaming flows; 4) includes documentation and code examples for each SDK; and 5) provides a migration plan and telemetry hooks for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A concise spec published in the SDK repo README with examples for Python/TS/Go
SDKs implement default retry presets with an opt-out configuration flag
Idempotency key API standardized across client idioms (sync/async/stream) with examples
Telemetry events emitted for retry attempts, budget exhaustion, id-key collisions, and stream resume events
Benchmarked e2e behavior for 95th pct latency and token-cost under typical interactive workloads (chat) attached to PR
proposed_defaults: Retry budget: 3 attempts per request for non-streaming generation (default), 1 retry for stream-start failures, 0 automatic retries for mid-stream connection failures (require explicit resume API)
Token-aware cap: per-request retry token cap = min(10_000 tokens, 3 * estimated_response_tokens). Clients should surface estimate_response_tokens parameter in high-level API (optional)

Backoff presets (base_ms, max_ms, factor, jitter):
  - fast: base=50ms, max=500ms, factor=1.5, jitter=full_random
  - balanced: base=150ms, max=1500ms, factor=2.0, jitter=decorrelated (see note)
  - conservative: base=500ms, max=5000ms, factor=2.5, jitter=full_random

Idempotency key format: opaque v1 keys (uuid4 hex) recommended for simple requests; for resumable streams recommend namespaced keys 'resumable:{session_id}:{chunk_index}' managed by SDK to avoid collisions
Default behavior for ambiguous HTTP 5xx vs 429: treat 429 as retryable under balanced/conservative presets, treat most 5xx as retryable once unless response contains non-retryable error code in body
notes_and_tradeoffs: Choosing fewer automatic stream retries avoids hidden cost amplification but places more burden on caller to implement resume logic. We recommend SDK helper APIs to mint and persist resume tokens to reduce friction.

Token-aware caps reduce runaway costs on large outputs but can cause early budget exhaustion for unexpectedly long generations; therefore we provide an opt-out and a visible telemetry event 'retry_budget_exhausted' so product teams can triage.

Full random jitter reduces synchronized retries but can increase tail latency; decorrelated jitter (per Exponential Backoff with full jitter decorrelation) gives a middle ground for 'balanced' preset.

Idempotency key namespaces increase safety but require SDKs to manage storage lifetimes for resumable keys when client apps don't persist them. We'll document a recommended TTL and garbage collection guidance.
We avoid forcing a single global default across all customers; presets will be documented and the hosted API will expose hints (Retry-After) which SDKs will honor if present.
examples:
Python example: minting id-key for resumable chat session:

from redwood_sdk import Client
client = Client()
# SDK helper to start resumable session
session = client.chat.start_resumable(session_name='support-123')
# session.id contains 'resumable:{uuid}:{0}' style key
# Send first chunk
client.chat.send_chunk(session_id=session.id, chunk=b'...')

# Client can later resume with session.id to continue streaming response without re-generating full output
Migration note: Customers on older SDKs with unlimited retries may see lower error masking after upgrade; we will include an opt-in 'legacy_retry_mode' config and a migration guide.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (docs + spec): publish spec and examples in sdk/docs and open RFC for review (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (SDK shallow implementation): add presets and id-key helpers behind feature flags in Python/TS/Go; add telemetry hooks (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (integration + tests): e2e tests with hosted API labs, benchmark runs for chat workloads, and update default flags (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (rollout): staggered enablement via telemetry thresholds, notify customers, and add console visualizations to spot budget exhaustion (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (follow-up): collect telemetry, adjust presets, and finalize defaults (ongoing)
review_log: 2025-01-30: RFC posted to #sdk-arch. Initial feedback from @maria and @chen: prefer 2 retries for small non-stream requests to balance UX.
2025-02-02: Design review with @Jamal on id-key UI surfaces in TS; suggested SDK-managed keys for resumable streams to prevent accidental duplication.
2025-02-04: Security review triage — no PII in id-keys; recommended TTL default of 7 days for resumable keys and support for customer-supplied KMS-wrapped persistence for enterprise customers.
